senses: A form of typesetting machine in which a complete line of characters is set at once.
The slug produced by such a machine, or matter composed in such lines.
ety: Genericized trademark; presumably from line + -o- + type.
examples: His days were spent at his linotype, where he refreshed himself occasionally from an ever-present gallon jug of cherry wine.

senses: To subject to a mass internet or email assault aimed at pushing a particular point of view.
ety: Back-formation from Freeper, from The Free Republic, a popular conservative forum.
examples: Hearsay even got "freeped." "Freepers," followers of a rightist Web site called Free Republic, orchestrated a "Freeper Call to Action."
Freeping is one of the reasons Internet surveys are useless as a gauge of public opinion because the results can reflect an organized campaign.

senses: A neurosurgical procedure that involves creating a hole within a cerebral ventricle for drainage.
ety: From ventriculo- + -stomy.

senses: A Japanese custom in which unattached individuals are introduced to each other to consider the possibility of marriage.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese お見合い (おみあい, o-miai).

senses: Having much or unlimited potential to develop in a certain way, especially in a desirable fashion.
ety: From pluri- + potent.

senses: Angostura bitters
A South American tree, with bark used in tradition medicine and as an ingredient in various bitters (but not Angostura bitters), Angostura trifoliata.
ety: From the former name of Ciudad Bolívar in Venezuela.

senses: someone who owns or operates a saloon (drinking establishment)
ety: From saloon + keeper.

senses: The monetary unit of Russia, Belarus and Transnistria, equal to 100 kopeks. (Russian: копе́йка (kopéjka), Belarusian: капе́йка (kapjéjka)).
ety: Borrowed from Russian рубль (rublʹ). Doublet of rubel and rubl.

senses: To run headfirst into a situation without prior planning or consideration.
ety: From Leeroy, after the Internet character Leeroy Jenkins.

senses: A supercar with such extreme performance and expense as to have exclusiveness even when compared with most other supercars.
ety: From hyper- + car.
examples: It’s one of fastest accelerating vehicles on the market today — at about $130,000, it is said to have the acceleration normally found in multimillion-dollar hypercars.

senses: An agricultural approach of using the interactive benefits from combining trees and shrubs with crops and/or livestock.
ety: By surface analysis, agro- + forestry, or, by surface analysis, agroforest + -ry.

senses: A person who plays the bassoon, a musical instrument in the woodwind family.
ety: From bassoon + -ist (“a person who uses something”).

senses: The point at which a firearm is aimed, typically identified by a red dot sight.
ety: From aim + point.

senses: A unit of measure of capacity, equal to one thousandth of a litre. Symbol: mL or ml.
ety: From milli- + litre, from French millilitre.
examples: A smaller mammal such as a dog has a sperm concentration of 300 000 000 per millilitre in an ejaculate of 8 ml in volume. Thus, each ejaculate will contain only 2 400 000 000 (24 × 10⁸).

senses: A leg (limb).
ety: From leg + -ie.
examples: Once when I was trying to make his position a little more comfortable, he said — "Never mind left leggie, mamma; it does not need any care. What would I give if poor right leggie was only like it once more!"

senses: One of the bullet-shaped protrusions on the bumpers of various 1950s cars, especially Cadillacs.
ety: After Dagmar, buxom American actress.

senses: To flop and droop, as a sign of aging or poor physical condition.
ety: Blend of flop + droop

senses: A ruck; a player who contests rucks.
ety: From ruck + -man.

senses: Having a covering of small knobs.
ety: From knobble + -y.

senses: polyvinyl alcohol fibers
ety: Introduced as a generic term by the Federal Trade Commission.

senses: A performer of folk music.
ety: From folk + -er.

senses: Entitled to elect a senator, or by senators.
ety: From Latin senātōrius + -al. Compare French sénatorial. By surface analysis, senator + -ial.

senses: To undo the act of seeing something; to erase the memory of having seen something, or otherwise reverse the effect of having seen something.
ety: From un- + see. Compare Middle English unseen, unsen (“to fail to see, be unable to see”).
examples: We have shown the world, and it cannot be unseen, it cannot be unknown, it cannot be forgotten, that Christianity cannot be defended on any ground where Infidelity can get an inch of fair play against it.
I have only seen the performance once; and I would not unsee it again if I could; but none the less I am a broken man after it.
Once you saw the face of a god in those jumbled blacks and whites, it was everybody out of the pool—you could never unsee it.

senses: A style of progressive metal music related to djent, with particular emphasis on manipulation of pitch, especially via bends and digital processing.
ety: Coined by Swedish metal band Vildhjarta.

senses: The ecology of the ancient past and of extinct organisms
ety: From paleo- + ecology.

senses: Not produced or derived by means of living organisms or their processes.
ety: From a- + biogenic.

senses: Any of several tropical American fish, of the family Loricariidae, popular in aquaria for their ability to clean tanks by eating algae growth.
ety: Shortened from plecostomus, from translingual Plecostomus.

senses: Any entity formed by joining two or more smaller entities together.
ety: The adjective (as “combined, united”) and noun are first attested in 1471, in Middle English, the verb in 1530; partly from Middle English conjugat(e) (“combined, united”), partly directly borrowed from New Latin coniugātus, the perfect passive participle of Latin coniugō (“to yoke together, combine; (New Latin) to conjugate, decline, inflect”) (see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3)), from con- (“with”) + iugō (“to join”). In Classical Latin, the word for conjugate (grammar) was dēclīnō, coniugō is a later back-formation from post-classical coniugātiō (“conjugation, declension”).

senses: Given freely; unearned.
Unjustified or unnecessary; not called for by the circumstances.
extraneous, interpolated.
ety: From Latin grātuītus (“free”), from Latin grātia (“favor”), grātus (“showing favor”).

senses: a strong, vertical salinity gradient; the (sometimes indistinct) border between layers of water that contain different amounts of salt
ety: From halo- + -cline.

senses: A car capable of flight.
ety: From air + car.

senses: A person who etches
ety: From etch + -er.

senses: Something nine inches long, or holding nine gallons, etc.
The digit 9 in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
ety: (1): From nine + -er.

senses: To rock soothingly.
ety: From the nursery rhyme Rock-a-bye Baby, previously recorded as "Hush-a-by(e) baby"; blend of rock + lullaby or rock + -abye (as in hush-a-bye, from -a- (connective interfix) + bye (“goodbye, bye-bye”)).
examples: It was a pleasant day, the boat rockabyed in the slight chop and by late afternoon I was more nearly asleep than awake.
And lying down that night why should I hear the Brownsville trains that long had rockabyed me?
Sprung rubber alarm clock: it bounced apart All over him: boingg: it loves him to death. The rubber loops contort, their moil and clench Rockabyeing him out of this world.

senses: A continuous process for manufacture of composite materials with constant cross section.
ety: Blend of pull + extrusion.
examples: During pultrusion, a collection of fibres are pulled through a resin bath and then through a heated die to cure the resin.

senses: Illuminated by starlight.
ety: From star + lit.
examples: The night continued beautifully clear and fine, and as we came into the fell country the outlines of the hills showed up dark against the starlit sky.

senses: A caravanserai; an inn.
ety: From Persian سرای (sarây, “courtyard; dwelling; palace”), with the sense as a seraglio via its use in Ottoman Turkish.

senses: Synonym of quinquennium: a five-year period, especially in reference to the first and second halves of calendrical decades.
A five-day period, especially a temperature average taken every five days.
A five-day division of the Chinese calendar, forming part of a solar term (Chinese: 候).
ety: From Ancient Greek πεντάς (pentás), from πέντε (pénte, “five”) + -άς (-ás, “-ad”). By surface analysis, pent- + -ad.

senses: All the pundits and commentators of the news media collectively.
ety: Probably a blend of commentary + proletariat, perhaps after proprietariat and salariat. Perhaps compare also secretariat.
examples: From Boston, a man who finally joined the commentariat by making his debut on CNBC’s Hardball, Esquire Magazine writer-at-large, Charlie Pierce!
The world, of course, is seen by the commentariat as a side issue, yet another diversion from his real work, which is to answer whatever questions they see fit to pose.

As the dust settles on the Supreme Court’s cataclysmically destabilizing term, a very persistent question has bubbled up among the law professor commentariat: How the hell are we going to teach all this?

senses: A painter or photographer who makes portraits.
ety: From portrait + -ist.
